title: ISS cabin air, ANITA-2 monthly average concentrations, March to September 2024
documentation: JSC Toxicology and Environmental Chemistry Group, Memorandum TOX-SW-2025-02, 'Toxicological Assessment of ISS Air and Water Quality: March 26, 2024 to September 23, 2024 (Increment 71) Including NG-21 Ingress and Boeing-CFT Ascent', dated October 21, 2025, 13 PDF pages; source PDF sha256 96356e314a1d88d29a5e6bb55d690f225aadb1709ce00827cac03a8b1c2ef245, 1,114,979 bytes
Table 2, PDF page 4; column positions checked against the rendered page image
instrument: ANITA-2 (Analyzing Interferometer for Ambient Air, FTIR, ESA), Columbus module, up to 48 analytes every 6 to 10 minutes; NASA selected it as the primary ISS trace contaminant monitor in early 2025 (report p. 3)
cadence: Monthly averages; 'increment_average' rows hold the last column

compound.description: As printed (PFP is octafluoropropane, DMCPS, TMS, HMCTS and OCTMS are siloxanes and silanols as abbreviated in the report)

value.description: Monthly average, mg/m3 per the table title; see notes for CO2

qualifier.description: not_detected (blank cell: 'Blank cells indicate that the compound was not detected during that month'); no_average_printed for a blank average cell

preprocessing: Transcribed from the PDF text layer (pdftotext from poppler, -layout) by transcribe_tox_inc71.py in this folder; no OCR and no reading of figures. Every printed cell is kept verbatim in 'printed'; 'value' is the number with thousands separators removed, empty when the cell is not a number; 'qualifier' names the non-numeric cases. The script stops if a table row does not have one cell per sample column. Blank cells are kept as rows with an empty value and a qualifier.
license: US Government work. NASA material is generally not subject to copyright in the United States (NASA media usage guidelines, https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/). Credit NASA as the source; no NASA logo or insignia is used (NASA-SOURCES.md section 4).
provenance_note: REPLAY of published NASA monthly averages.
is_not: Monthly means, not the 6 to 10 minute instrument series (that series is not public).

consumers.component: simulators/habitat CO, ammonia and VOC feeds
consumers.use: Monthly anchor levels for the SIM generators (CO 1.52 to 2.32 mg/m3; ammonia 0.03 mg/m3 in two months, otherwise not detected).
Nominal values far below the SMACs (CO 15 ppm, ammonia 3 ppm in environment-hazards.json): replay must stay at info.

notes: The CO2 row reads 2.1 to 2.5 under a table titled mg/m3. Those values match the ppCO2 range in mmHg that the report plots in Figure 2, so the CO2 unit is not asserted here; do not use that row as mg/m3.
